subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the point of contact of the tangent x − 2y − 5 = 0 and the circle x² + y² = 5.

mark_split.label: Write the point of contact formula

insider_note: The formula has a minus sign in front and n in the denominator, so work out the sign of each coordinate on its own — do not assume the two come out with the same sign. Here n = −5 with l = 1 gives x = +1, while the same n = −5 with m = −2 gives y = −2. Writing the signs one at a time is safer than doing it in the head.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the point of contact formula
steps.margin_note: One mark. Read l, m, n from the line as written, and r² from the circle.
steps.memory_tip: Point of contact of lx + my + n = 0 with x² + y² = r² is (−lr²/n, −mr²/n).
lines: Compare x − 2y − 5 = 0 with lx + my + n = 0
steps.why: The point of contact is the foot of the perpendicular from the centre, and for a circle centred at the origin that works out to (−lr²/n, −mr²/n). It is only valid when the line really touches the circle.
common_mistakes: Using r = 5 in place of r² = 5.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Check the answer by putting it back into both the line and the circle.
steps.memory_tip: Both coordinates have −5 underneath, so both signs flip once more.
steps.why: A check: 1 − 2(−2) − 5 = 1 + 4 − 5 = 0, so the point is on the line, and 1² + (−2)² = 5, so it is on the circle. A point on both is the point of contact.
common_mistakes: Getting y = 2 by cancelling only one of the two minus signs.
